items.title: Reflection symmetry of the spherical differential expression

source.edition: Samplinglib original shared mathematical supplement, 2026-11-18; Lean 4.33.0
source.anchor: Original reflection identity stated in runs/20261118-sphere-antipodal-generator/source-statement.txt. The linked pinned source supplies the existing extrinsic operator definition.
source.attribution: Original Samplinglib derivation from the pinned operator definition and Mathlib derivative transport. The linked file defines the operator; it is not presented as an external proof of this new bundled statement.

items.statement: Let A(x)=-x on E=R^I, where I is finite. For every real-valued ambient function f and every w,h∈E, the first derivative of f∘A at w applied to h equals -Df(-w)[h]. The existing extrinsic spherical differential expression commutes with reflection: L_S(f∘A)(w)=L_Sf(-w). These equalities use the total Mathlib derivative operators. In the classical smooth setting at unit points, they give the familiar reflection symmetry of the spherical generator.
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality, and E is the real Euclidean space with coordinates indexed by I.
f:E→R and w∈E are arbitrary; the first identity quantifies every direction h∈E. No smoothness, unit-norm or positive-dimension premise is imposed on the total-operator identity.
The radial correction uses max(|I|−1,0), implemented by natural-number subtraction before conversion to R.

obligations.label: Transport the actual first derivative and extrinsic sphere expression under negation

bindings.boundary: This is a transport identity for total ambient differential expressions. It does not assert that an arbitrary f has classical derivatives, nor construct an intrinsic Laplace–Beltrami operator, diffusion, invariant measure, evolution-equation solution or log-Sobolev inequality. Classical sphere applications separately supply C2 tests and unit points.
